root_causes: Text/embedding memory (episodes, topic_facts, semantic_triples, entities) never captured the small on-screen '精魄' pickup UI text for 地狼 or 鼠弩手 -- captions describe generic combat/loot instead, so pure-SQL/semantic_search retrieval cannot solve this question at all

The only boss name that IS present in text (沙二郎, from NPC dialogue) is a hallucination-detection distractor; rollouts that never called clip_qa (rollout 1, rollout 4) both converged on the textually-salient-but-wrong 沙二郎

Rollouts that did call clip_qa but chose time windows that excluded one of the two true clue intervals (rollout 0 started its first window at 10200, after the ~10151-10162 pickup; rollout 3 skipped the 10210-10550 gap containing the ~10480 pickup) still produced wrong answers because the sub-agent simply never saw the missing evidence

Even when clip_qa correctly read the on-screen spirit name (e.g. rollout 0's window did see 地狼·精魄 clearly, rollout 3's window did see 鼠弩手·精魄 clearly), the main agent sometimes overrode or misattributed the sub-agent's finding (rollout 0 kept 沙二郎 despite clip_qa reporting no spirit in that window; rollout 3 conflated 'boss fought' identity with 'boss encountered second')

Only rollout 2 called clip_qa broadly enough (4 separate windows spanning both true intervals) to land on the correct pair, though even it had one hallucinated visual read (a false 'Earth Wolf' claim at 10290-10390) that happened not to change its final answer
what_worked: Rollout 2's strategy of issuing multiple, overlapping clip_qa calls across the full 10120-10810s span, rather than 1-2 narrow windows, increased the odds of covering both true clue intervals and cross-checking each boss/spirit pairing

Rollout 2 also actively re-queried clip_qa when an earlier answer looked inconsistent (checking whether the gate-fight aftermath in 10720-10810 had a spirit, and finding none), which correctly ruled out a distractor boss
transferable_lessons: For 'which spirit/reward did boss X give' questions in this game-footage domain, text memory (captions/entities/facts) frequently omits small on-screen pickup banners entirely -- clip_qa/visual verification is not optional, it is required, even when SQL/semantic_search return plausible-looking hits

When a question lists specific named entities as multiple-choice options, check whether each name actually appears in the entities/semantic_triples tables before trusting it -- a name's mere presence in the DB (e.g. via unrelated dialogue) does not mean it is the correct answer; this is exactly the hallucination-detection trap

When using clip_qa to scan a sequence of 'first boss, second boss' events, sample windows that fully cover the entire relevant span (or verify no gap exists) rather than 2 narrow, non-adjacent windows -- a boss/spirit event sitting in an unsampled gap will simply never be found

When a clip_qa sub-call explicitly reports 'no spirit/reward visible in this interval', trust that negative result rather than overriding it with a text-derived guess to fill in a forced-choice answer
open_questions: Whether the game's actual boss encountered at ~10140-10160s is really called 'Earth Wolf' as several clip_qa sub-calls claimed, or whether that boss-identity label was itself a visual misread (its Chinese boss-name banner was never independently confirmed in this investigation, only the resulting 鼠弩手/精魄 pickup banner) -- does not affect scoring since only the spirit names mattered
